issuer: Reserve Bank of India
section_path: 1. Applicability and layers > 1.1 Layered structure
chunk_text: NBFCs are regulated in four layers according to size, activity and perceived riskiness: Base Layer (NBFC-BL), Middle Layer (NBFC-ML), Upper Layer (NBFC-UL) and a notionally empty Top Layer. Regulatory requirements are cumulative: an NBFC in a higher layer must comply with the requirements of the lower layers as well as those specific to its own layer.

section_path: 2. Asset classification and provisioning > 2.1 NPA recognition norm
chunk_text: An asset is classified as a non-performing asset when principal or interest remains overdue for more than 90 days. Base Layer NBFCs transitioned to the 90-day norm through a glide path: overdue for more than 150 days by March 2024, more than 120 days by March 2025 and more than 90 days by March 2026.

section_path: 2. Asset classification and provisioning > 2.2 Special Mention Accounts
chunk_text: Lenders must identify incipient stress by classifying accounts as Special Mention Accounts: SMA-0 where principal or interest is overdue for 1 to 30 days, SMA-1 for 31 to 60 days and SMA-2 for 61 to 90 days. Classification is done as part of the day-end process and upgradation of an NPA to standard requires repayment of all arrears of interest and principal.
